changelog: Add a core principle warning against cutting between a verb and its essential complement and describing what a GOOD cut looks like, to address the primary finding that the prompt underestimates how tightly verbs bind to complements.
findings: The prompt underestimates how tightly verbs bind to their complements: it permits cuts that separate a predicate from its essential object/resultative/degree/particle, producing standalone fragments whose meaning is completed, negated, or reversed by the continuation.

edits.was: - Evaluate discourse connectors and coordination: conjunctions and reporting/con
edits.now: - Avoid cutting between a verb and its essential complement (object, resultative

diagnosis.why: Inserting a rule to avoid cutting between verbs and their essential complements made the model less likely to split verb–object/resultative chunks, giving small average gains (largest in the shortest latency bin ≤3) but also shifting many cuts so that punctuation or quotation marks became isolated fragments — those shifted cuts produced the large negative tail movements and left the net effect marginal.
diagnosis.lesson: Respect verb–complement binding but avoid moving cuts in a way that leaves punctuation/quotes or other tiny tokens as isolated pieces; ensure punctuation stays attached to the unit it punctuates when enforcing verb-complement constraints.
